G4500.def:
ῥοιζηδόν
adv. (ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow),
with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): 2Pe 3:10.†
(AS)

G4501.def:
ῥομφαία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶב ;]
a large broad sword, used by the Thracians (see DB, iv, 634); then generally (in LXX used interchangeably with μάχαιρα, which see), a sword: Ap 1:16 2:12, 16 6:8 19:15, 21; metaphorically, Lc 2:35.†
(AS)

G4505.def:
ῥύμη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX: Is 15:3 (רְחֹב), Pv 31:23 א, Tob.13:18, Sir.9:7 א1* ;]
__1. in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers.
__2. In late Greek (as in Macedonian, see Kennedy, Sources, 15), a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town, Mt 6:2, Lc 14:21 At 9:11 12:10 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 488).†
(AS)

G4506.def:
ῥύομαι
[in LXX chiefly for נָצַל hi., also for גָּאַל, פָּלַט pi., etc. ;]
to draw to oneself, hence, to rescue, deliver: with accusative of person(s), Mt 27:43, 2Pe 2:7; id. before ἀπό, Mt 6:13, Lc 11:4 (Rec., R, mg.), 2Tm 4:18; before ἐκ, Rm 7:24, 2Co 1:10, Cl 1:13, 1Ts 1:10, 2Tm 3:11, 2Pe 2:9; absol., ὁ ῥυύμενος, the deliverer, Rm 11:26. Passive: before ἀπό, Rm 15:31, 2Ts 3:2; before ἐκ, Lc 1:74, 2Tm 4:17.†
(AS)

G4507.def:
ῥυπαρία, -ας, ἡ
(ῥυπαρός)
filthiness: metaphorically, of moral defile­ment, Tg 1:21.†
(AS)

G4508.def:
ῥυπαρός, -ά, -όν
(ῥύπος), [in LXX: Zc 3:4-5, (3-4) (צוֹא)* ;]
filthy, dirty: of old, shabby clothing (Za, l.with), Tg 2:2; metaphorically, of moral defilement, Ap 22:11.†
(AS)

G4509.def:
ῥύπος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Is 4:4 (צוֹאָה), Jó 14:4 (טָמֵא), etc. ;]
dirt, filth: 1Pe 3:21.†
(AS)

G4510.def:
ῥυπόω, -ῶ
(ῥύπος),
to make filthy: Ap 22:11 Rec. (AV, tr. as = ῥυπάω, to be filthy).†
(AS)

G4511.def:
ῥύσις, -εως, ἡ
(ῥέω), [in LXX chiefly for זוֹב ;]
a flowing, issue: τ. αἵματος, Mc 5:25, Lc 8:43-44.†
(AS)

G4512.def: a fold or pucker in the face, a wrinkle , Lat. ruga, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G4513.def:
Roman, a Roman , (Polybius Historicus), etc.; adverb -κῶς, in Latin , [variant datesAnthology Palantina
(ML)

G4517.def:
ῥώννυμι
[in LXX: 2Ma.9:20 2Mac 11:21 2Mac 11:28 2Mac 11:33 2Mac 11:1-38; 3Ma.6:1-41 * ;]
to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): At 15:29 23:30 Rec., R, mg.†
(AS)

G4518.def:
σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.with, WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי),
sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: Mt 27:46, Mc 15:34 (Sl 22:2, Heb. עָזַב).†
ζαφθανεί (cf. Heb. עָזַב),
zaphthanei: Mt 27:46 (WH, mg., for Rec. σεβαχθανεί, which see; "probably an attempt to reproduce the Heb. as disting from Aram. forms," WE, Notes, 21; cf. also Dalman, Words, 53 f.).†
(AS)

G4519.def:
σαβαώθ indecl.,
[in LXX for צָבָא, chiefly in Isaiah (in other places, the phrase is also rendered by κύριος παντοκράτωρ, κ. τῶν δυνάμεων; see DB, iii, 137 f.) ;]
Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (see DB, l.with): Rm 9:29 (LXX), Ja 54.†
(AS)

G4520.def:
σαββατισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath, Êx 16:30, al.),
a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaphorically, as in Mishna (Zorell, see word), Hb 4:9.†
(AS)

G4521.def:
σάββατον, -ου, τό (Aram. שַׁבָּתָא, transliterated σάββατα, and this being mistaken for a pl., the sing. σάββατον was formed from it), and σάββατα, -ων, τά
[in LXX for שַׁבָּת, שַׁבָּתוֹן ;]
__1. the seventh day of the week, the sabbath
__(a) the sing. form -ον, τὸ σ.: Mt 12:8, Mc 2:27, Lc 6:5, al.; ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ σ. (in LXX, Êx 20:8, al., usually τῶν σ., see infr.), Lc 13:16 14:5; ὁδὸς σαββάτου, At 1:12 (cf. Mt 24:29); dative, of time (τῷ) σ., Lc 6:9 14:1; ἐν (τῷ) σ., Mt 12:2, Lc 6:7, Jo 5:16, al.; accusative, of duration, τὸ σ., Lc 23:56; κατὰ πᾶν σ., At 13:27 15:21 18:4; pl., σ. τρία, At 17:2 R, txt. (but see infr.);
__(b) as most frequently in LXX (see Swete, Mk., 17; Thackeray, Gr., 35) the pl. form, τὰ σ. (see supr. on the Aram. form. There is also an analogy in the names of other festivals, τ. ἐγκαίνια, ἄζυμα, etc.): Mt 28:1, Cl 2:16; ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν σ. (Êx 20:8, al.), Lc 4:16, At 13:14 16:13; dative pl. (in LXX -τοις, but 1Ma.2:38 as in NT) by metaplasmus (El., § 9, 3), σάββασι, Mt 12:1, 5 12:10-12 Mc 1:21 2:23 3:2, 4, Lc 4:31 6:2.
__2. seven days, a week;
__(a) the sing. form: πρώτη σαββάτσυ, Mc 16:9; δὶς τοῦ σ. (Bl., § 35, 4; 36, 13), Lc 18:12; κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου, 1Co 16:2; pl., σ. τρία, At 17:2 R, mg. (but see supr.);
__(b) the pl. form: ἡ μία τῶν σ. (where the genitive = μετὰ τά; Soph., Lex., 43a), Mt 28:1, Mc 16:2, Lc 24:1, Jo 20:1, 19, At 20:7
(AS)

G4522.def:
σαγήνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם ;]
a drag-net, seine: Mt 13:47.†
SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), δίκτυον (AS)

G4524.def:
Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, see supr., see word Σαδδουκαῖος)
Sadoc, Zadok: Mt 1:14.†
(AS)

G4525.def:
σαίνω
__1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn.
__2. Metaphorical, of persons, with accusative, to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., 1Ts 3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, see ICC, and M, Th., in l).†
(AS)

G4526.def:
σάκκος also written σάκος, -ου, ὁ
(cf. Heb. שַׂק, which it renders in LXX),
__1. a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: Ap 6:12.
__2. Anything made of sackcloth;
__(a) a sack (Gn 42:25, al.);
__(b) a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: Mt 11:21, Lc 10:13, Ap 11:3.†
(AS)

G4527G.def:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח),
Sala, Shalah: Lc 3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Lc 3:35.†
(AS)

G4527H.def:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח),
Sala, Shalah: Lc 3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Lc 3:35.†
(AS)

G4529.def:
Σαλαμίς, -ῖνσς, ἡ
Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: At 13:5.†
(AS)

G4530.def:
Σαλείμ, τό indecl.,
Salim: Jo 3:23 (see Westc., in l; DB, iii, 354).†
(AS)

G4531.def:
σαλεύω
(σάλος), [in LXX for מוֹט, זוּעַ, etc. ;]
prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, Mt 11:7, Lc 7:24; a house, Lc 6:48, At 4:31 16:26; the earth, Hb 12:26; the heavenly bodies, Mt 24:29, Mc 13:25, Lc 21:26; of a vessel shaken in filling, Lc 6:38. Metaphorical,
__(a) to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., Hb 12:27;
__(b) with accusative of person(s), to cast down from a sense of security and happiness: At 2:25 (LXX);
__(with) to unsettle or drive away: pass., before ἀπὸ τ. νοός, 2Ts 2:2;
__(d) to stir up: τ. ὄχλους, At 17:13.†
(AS)

G4533.def:
Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן),
Salmon: Mt 1:4-5, Lc 3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).†
(AS)

G4534.def:
Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ
Salmone, a promontory of Crete: At 27:7.†
(AS)

G4535.def:
σάλος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for מוֹט, etc. ;]
in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: Lc 21:25.†
(AS)

G4536.def:
σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;]
a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: 1Co 14:8, Hb 12:19, Ap 1:10 4:1 8:2, 6 8:11 9:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Mt 24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, 1Ts 4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., 1Co 15:52.†
(AS)

G4537.def:
σαλπίζω
[in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;]
to sound a trumpet: Ap 8:6 ff. Ap 9:1, 13 10:7 11:15; metaphorically, Mt 6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: 1Co 15:52.†
(AS)

G4538.def:
σαλπιστής
(so Inscr. and late writers for Mt. σαλπιγκτής), οῦ, ὁ,
a trumpeter: Ap 18:22.†
(AS)

G4540.def:
Σαμαρία (Rec. -άρεια), -ας, ἡ (Heb. שֹׁמְרוֹן; Aram. שָׁמְרַיִן),
Samaria;
__(a) the city: At 8:5 (and perhaps also At 8:9, 14);
__(b) the region: Lc 17:11, Jo 4:4-5, 7, At 1:8 8:1 (and perhaps also At 8:9, 14) At 9:31 15:3.†
(AS)

G4541.def:
Σαμαρείτης
(-ίτης, Τ; see WH, App., 154; BI., § 3, 4), -ον, ό,
a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (see: Σαμαρία): Mt 10:5, Lc 9:52 10:33 17:16, Jo 4:9, 39-40, At 8:25; as an opprobrious epithet, Jo 8:48.†
(AS)

G4542.def:
Σαμαρεῖτις (-ῖτις, T, see supr.), -ιδος, ἡ
__1. in FlJ (B.J., i, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria.
__2. a Samaritan woman: Jo 4:9.†
(AS)

G4543.def:
Σαμοθρᾴκη
(-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ
Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: At 16:11.†
(AS)

G4544.def:
Σάμος, -ου, ἡ
Samos, an island in the Ægean: At 20:15.†
(AS)

G4545.def:
Σαμουήλ, ὁ indecl.
(in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb. שְׁמוּאֵל),
Samuel (1Rs 1:20, al.): At 3:24 13:20, Hb 11:32.†
(AS)

G4546.def:
Σαμψών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שִׁמְשׁוֹן),
Samson (Jz 13:1-25 ff.): Hb 11:32.†
(AS)

G4547.def:
σανδάλιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian), [in LXX: Js 9:5, Is 20:2 (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, which see), Jdth.10:4 16:9 * ;]
a sandal: Mc 6:9, At 12:8.†
(AS)

G4548.def:
σανίς, -ίδος, ἡ
[in LXX: Ct 8:9, Eze.27:5 (לוּחַ) * ;]
a board, plank: At 27:44
(AS)

G4549G.def:
Σαούλ, ὁ indecl.
(in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb. שָׁאוּל)
Saul;
__(a) the King of Israel: At 13:21;
__(b) the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): At 9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14.†
(AS)

G4549H.def:
Σαούλ, ὁ indecl.
(in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb. שָׁאוּל)
Saul;
__(a) the King of Israel: At 13:21;
__(b) the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): At 9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14.†
(AS)

G4550.def:
σαπρός, -ά -όν
[in Sm.: Lv 27:14, 33 * ;]
rotten, corrupt, bad, worth­less: of trees and fruit (opposite to ἀγαθός, καλός), Mt 7:17-18 12:33 Lc 6:43; of fish, Mt 13:48.
Metaphorical, in moral sense: λόγος σ., Ef 4:29. "In Hellenistic . . . it became a synonym for αἰσχρός or κακός," MM, xxii.†
(AS)

G4552.def:
σάπφειρος, -ου, ἡ
[in LXX for סַפִּיר ;]
sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli): Ap 21:19.†
(AS)

G4553.def:
σαργάνη, -ης, ἡ
__1. a plaited rope (Æsch.).
__2. a hamper, a basket made of ropes: 2Co 11:33.†
(AS)

G4554.def:
Σάρδεις, -εων, αἱ
Sardis, the chief city of Lydia: Ap 1:11 3:1, 4
(AS)

G4556.def:
σάρδιον, -ον, τ
[in LXX for אֹדֶם, Êx 28:17, al.; also for שֹׁהַם ;]
the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): Ap 4:3 21:20.†
(AS)

G4557.def:
σαρδόνυξ (L, σαρδιόνυξ), -υχος, ὁ
(σάρδιον, ὄνυξ),
sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: Ap 21:20.†
(AS)

G4558.def:
Σάρεπτα, -ων (Ob 20), τά (Heb. צָרְפַת),
Sarepta, a city of Sidon: Lc 4:26.†
(AS)

G4559.def:
σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (σάρξ)
(seel. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7)
= Lat. carnalis, i.e.
__(a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Rm 15:27, 1Co 9:11;
__(b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, 1Pe., 133): 1Co 3:3, 2Co 1:12 10:4, 1Pe 2:11.†
SYN.: σάρκινος (which see), ψυχικός; cf. Tr., Syn., §§ LXXi, LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184 f.; Vau. on Rm 7:14 (AS)

G4560.def:
σάρκινος, -η, -ον
(σάρξ), [in LXX: 2Cr 32:8, Eze.11:19 36:26 (בָּשָׂר), Et 4:17, Pv 24:23 (Pv 29:27) * ;]
= Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; see Tr., Syn., § LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., see MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Rm 7:14, 1Co 3:1, 2Co 3:3, Hb 7:16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except 2Co 3:3, but the evidence is decisive against it.)†
SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v (AS)

G4561.def:
σάρξ, σαρκός, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;]
flesh;
__1. as in cl. generally,
__(a) prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: 1Co 15:39, 2Co 12:7, Gl 6:13, al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, 1Co 5:50; σ. καὶ ὀστέα, Lc 24:39; pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), Ap 17:16 19:18; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. with (cf. κατεσθίειν, 4Ki.9:36, al., and βιβρώσκειν, frequently in l.); metaphorically, Tg 5:3; mystically, φ. (τρώγειν) τὴν σ. τοῦ υἱοῦ τ. ἀνθρώπου, Jo 6:52-56;
__(b) Of the whole substance of the body, = σῶμα: At 2:26 (LXX), 31, 2Co 12:7, Gl 4:14, Ef 5:29; μία σ., Mc 10:8; εἰς σ. μίαν (Gn 2:24), Mt 19:5, Mc 10:8, 1Co 6:16, Ef 5:31; hence, of the material as opposite to the immaterial part of man (cf. Lft., Notes, 88): opposite to πνεῦμα, 1Co 5:5, 2Co 7:1, Cl 2:5, 1Pe 3:18, 4:6; to ψύχη, At 2:31, Rec.; of the present life, ἐν (τῇ) σ., Rm 7:5, Gl 2:20, Fp 1:22, 24 1Pe 4:2; of Christ's life on earth, αἱ ἡμέραι τ. σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, Hb 5:7; of things pertaining to the body, ἐν (τῇ) σ., Gl 6:12, 13 Fp 3:3, 4.
__2. As in Heb. idiom,
__(a) of a living creature: πᾶσα σ. (Heb. כָּל־בָּשָׂר; cf. Bl., §47, 9), Mt 24:22, Mc 13:20, 1Pe 1:24; esp. of man and his mortality (Psa.55 (56):5, Sir.28:5, al.), Jo 1:14; πᾶσα σ. (see supr.), Lc 3:6, Jo 17:2, At 2:17, ἐν σ., 1Jo.4:2, 1Tm 3:16;
__(b) of natural origin and relationship (Gn 2:24, Is 58:7, al.): τέκνα τῆς σ., Rm 9:8; κατὰ σάρκα, ib. 3, 5, 1Co 10:18, Gl 4:23, 29; ἡ σ. μου, Rm 11:14 (cf. Jz 9:2, 2Rs 5:1, al.).
__3. Of the physical nature as subject to sensation and desire (Plut.),
__(a) without any ethical disparagement: Rm 7:18 13:14; opposite to πνεῦμα, Mt 26:41, Mc 14:38; τ. θέλημα τῆς σ., Jo 1:13; ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σ., 1Jo 2:16; pl., 2Pe 2:18; παθεῖν σαρκί, 1Pe 4:1;
__(b) in ethical sense, esp. in Pauline Epp., of the flesh as the seat and vehicle of sinful desires: opposite to νοῦς, Rm 7:25; to πνεῦμα, Rm 8:4-9, 12, 13, Gl 5:16, 17 19 6:8 (cf. DB, ii, 14f.; iv, 165f.; Cremer, 844ff.).
(AS)

G4563.def:
σαρόω, -ῶ
late form of σαίρω,
to sweep: with accusative, Lc 15:8; pass., Mt 12:44, Lc 11:25.†
(AS)

G4565.def:
Σάρων, -ωνος (accusative -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן),
the plain of Sharon: At 9:35.†
(AS)

G4567.def:
Σατανᾶς, -ᾶ
(so also Sir 21:30, but in 3Ki.11:14, σατάν indecl.; Heb. שָׂטָן; Aram. סָטָנָא, whence the inflected Gk. form), ό,
Satan (i.e. the adversary, as in LXX, ll. with): Mt 4:10 12:26, Mc 1:13 3:23, 26 4:15 Lc 10:18 11:18 13:16 22:3, 31, Jo 13:27, At 5:3 26:18, Rm 16:20, 1Co 5:5 7:5, 2Co 2:11 11:14, 1Ts 2:18, 2Ts 2:9, 1Tm 1:20 5:15, Ap 2:9, 13 2:24 3:9 12:9 20:2, 7; addressed in person of Peter, Mt 16:23 Mc 8:33; ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ, 2Co 12:7.†
(AS)

G4568.def:
σάτον, -ου, τό
(Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), [in LXX: Ag 2:17 (16)* ;]
a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Mt 13:33, Lc 13:21.†
(AS)

G4569G.def:
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, which see),
Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: At 7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8 9:11, 22 9:24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1-2, 7 13:9.†
(AS)

G4569H.def:
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, which see),
Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: At 7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8 9:11, 22 9:24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1-2, 7 13:9.†
(AS)

G4570.def:
σβέννυμι
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבָה ;]
of fire or things on fire, to quench: with accusative, Mt 12:20, Ef 6:16, Hb 11:34; pass., Mt 25:8, Mc 9:48, [44, 46]. Metaphorical (cf. Ct 8:7, 4Ma.16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, 1Ts 5:19.†
ζβέννυμι, for σβ-, 1Ts 5:19 T (see WH, Notes, 148).†
(AS)

G4573.def:
σεβάζομαι
(σέβας, reverential awe), [in Aq.: Os 10:5 * ;]
__1. to fear (Hom).
__2. In later writers, = σέβομαι, to worship: Rm 1:25
(AS)

G4574.def:
σέβασμα, -τος, τό
(σεβάζομαι), [in LXX: Wis.14:20 15:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 * ;]
an object of worship: At 17:23, 2Ts 2:4.†
(AS)

G4575.def:
σεβαστός, -ή, -όν (σεβάζομαι)
__1. reverend, august.
__2. In late writers, with reference to the Roman Imperial name;
__(a) ὁ Σ., Augustus, i.e. the Roman Emperor: At 25:21, 25;
__(b) Augustan: σπείρα σ., At 27:1 (See further, Deiss., BS, 218.) †
(AS)

G4576.def:
σέβω
[in LXX (chiefly for יָרֵא, Js 4:24, al.) and NT always mid., σέβομαι, exc. 4Ma.5:24 ;]
to worship: with accusative of person(s), Mt 15:9, Mc 7:7, At 18:13 19:27; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, At 16:14 18:7; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, At 13:43, 50 17:4, 17 (cf. προσήλυτος).†
(AS)

G4577.def:
σειρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX: Jz 16:13-14, 19 (מַחְלָפָה), Pv 5:22 (חֶבֶל) * ;]
__1. (a) a cord;
__(b) a chain (cf. Pr., l.with): σειραὶ ζόφου, 2Pe 2:4, Rec., R, mg. (see: σειρός).
__2. a lock of hair (Jg, ll. with).†
(AS)

G4578.def:
σεισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(σείω), [in LXX chiefly for רַעַשׁ ;]
a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: Mt 8:24; esp. an earthquake: Mt 24:7 27:54 28:2, Mc 13:8, Lc 21:11, At 16:26, Ap 6:12 8:5 11:13, 19 16:18.†
(AS)

G4579.def:
σείω
[in LXX chiefly for רָעַשׁ ;]
to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, Hb 12:26 (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, Mt 27:51 (LXX); συκῆ, Ap 6:13. Metaphorical, to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: Mt 21:10 28:4 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).†
(AS)

G4582.def:
σελήνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for יָרֵחַ (Gn 37:9, al.), also for לְבָנָה; (Ct 6:9(10), ?Is 24:23 30:26) ;]
the moon: Mt 24:29, Mc 13:24, Lc 21:25, At 2:20" (LXX), 1Co 15:41, Ap 6:12 8:12 12:1 21:23.†
(AS)

G4583.def:
σεληνιάζω
(σελήνη),
act, in Manetho (Caren., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι,
to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): Mt 4:24 17:15.†
(AS)

G4585.def:
σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;]
fine wheaten flour: Ap 18:13.†
(AS)

G4586.def:
σεμνός, -ή, -όν
(σέβομαι), [in LXX: Pv 6:8 8:6 15:26, 2Ma.6:11 2Mac 6:28 2Mac 8:15, 4Ma.5:36 4Mac 7:15 4Mac 17:5 * ;]
__1. reverend, august, venerable, in cl. of the gods and also of human beings.
__2. grave, serious; of persons: 1Tm 3:8 3:11, Tt 2:2; of things: Fp 4:8 (see Tr., Syn., § xcii; Cremer, 37; MM, xxii).†
(AS)

G4587.def:
σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ
(σεμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:12 * ;]
gravity: 1Tm 2:2 3:4 (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), Tt 2:7.†
(AS)

G4591.def:
σημαίνω
(σῆμα, a sign), [in LXX for רוּעַ hi., תָּקַע, etc. ;]
to give a sign, signify, indicate: with accusative of thing(s), At 25:27, Ap 1:1 (cf. MM, xxii); with accusative and inf., At 11:28; before quæst. indir., Jo 12:33 18:32 21:19.†
(AS)

G4592.def:
σημεῖον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for אוֹת ;]
a sign, mark, token;
__(a) of that which distinguishes a person or thing from others: Mt 26:48 Lc 2:12, 2Ts 3:17 (cf. Deiss., LAE, 153.2); before genitive epexeg., Rm 4:11; with genitive obj., Mt 24:8, 30, 2Co 12:12; with genitive subj., Mt 16:3;
__(b) a sign of warning or admonition: Mt 12:39 16:4, Lc 2:34 11:29-30, 1Co 14:22;
__(with) a sign portending future events (Soph., Plat. al.): Mc 13:4, Lc 21:7, 11 21:25, At 2:19, Ap 12:1, 3 15:1;
__(d) of miracles and wonders (MM, xxii), regarded as signs of a divine authority: Mt 12:38-39 16:1, 4 Mc 8:11-12 Lc 11:16, 29 23:8, Jo 2:11, 18 2:23 4:54 6:30 10:41 12:18, At 4:16, 22; pl., Mc 16:17, 20, Jo 2:11, 23 3:2 6:2, 14 6:26 7:31 9:16 11:47 12:37 20:30, At 8:6, 1Co 1:22 (Lft., Notes, 162); the same ascribed to false teachers and demons: Mt 24:24, Mc 13:22, 2Ts 2:9, Ap 13:13-14 16:14 19:20; σ. καὶ τέρατα (τ. καὶ σ.; cf. Tr., Syn., § xci), Mt 24:24, Mc 13:22, Jo 4:48, At 2:19, 43 4:30 5:12 6:8 7:36 14:3 15:12, Rm 15:19, 2Ts 2:9; id. before καὶ δυνάμεις, 2Co 12:12, Hb 2:4; σ. καὶ δυνάμεις, At 8:13; δ. καὶ τ. καὶ σ., At 2:22; σ. διδόναι, Mt 24:24, Mc 13:22.†
(AS)

G4593.def:
σημειόω, -ῶ
(σημεῖον), [in LXX: Sl 4:6 (נָשָׂא)* ;]
to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2Ts 3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).†
(AS)

G4594.def:
σήμερον (Att.. τήμερον),
adv., [in LXX for יוֹם ;]
to-day: Mt 6:11, Lc 4:21, At 4:9, al.; opposite to αὔριον, Mt 6:30, Lc 12:28, Tg 4:13; χθὲς καὶ σ. καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, Hb 13:8; ἡ σ. ἡμέρα, At 20:20; ἕως (ἄχρι) τῆς σ. ἡμέρας, Rm 11:8, 2Co 3:14; μέχρι (ἕως) τῆς σ. (sc. ἡμέρας), Mt 11:23 27:8; as subst., τὸ σ., Hb 3:13; id. in appos., ὁρίζει ἡμὶραν, σ., Hb 4:7 R, mg., (see Westc., in l)
(AS)

G4595.def:
σήπω
[in LXX; Sl 38:5 (מָקַק ni.), Jó 33:21 (כָּלָה) Jó 40:7, Sir.14:19, al. ;]
to make corrupt: 2 pf. act, with mid, sense (see M, Pr., 154), σέσηπεν, has perished, become corrupted, Tg 5:2.†
(AS)

G4596.def:
σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; see Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν
(οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk),
silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Ap 18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†
(AS)

G4597.def:
σής σητός (late genitive for cl. σεός), ὁ,
[in LXX: Jó 4:19, Is 50:9 (עָשׁ), Is 51:8 (סָס), al. ;]
a moth, clothes moth: Mt 6:19-20, Lc 12:33.†
(AS)
